rationale: Facilitated planning has randomised support (claim c2) and matches what farmers say they act on (claim c3). The practice's question is whether its own vets can deliver it and whether measures are adopted and kept on its clients' farms, which is an implementation question. Adoption is observed, not reported (claim c4). A second cluster-randomised trial was considered and refused.
alternatives: Cluster-randomised trial of planning visits against usual advice (refused: too few herds and vet hours, and the effect has already been shown)
Farmer questionnaire on barriers (refused as the main design: self-report overstates practice)
Leaflet campaign (refused: generic advice is what farmers ignore)
whyNotMoreComplex: A trial would need more herds and vets than the practice has and would repeat a question already answered; the local question is delivery and adoption.

decision.statement: Deliver facilitated biosecurity planning visits to consenting client dairy herds from January to June 2027, with baseline and six-month observation of five core measures and a record of delivery fidelity.
decision.question: How should the practice try to raise biosecurity adoption on its dairy clients' farms?

criteria.text: A facilitated plan with a few agreed priorities raised observed adoption in comparable herds.
Too few client herds agree to take part to learn anything about delivery.

gates.requirement: Vet time for planning visits and observation
gates.evidence: Investigator constraint entered on the Problem screen: two practice vets can each give one half-day a week from January to June 2027

gates.requirement: Written agreement of participating farmers, including consent to unannounced observation visits

decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c2 to c4; farmer agreement is unknown until recruitment starts.

summary: Implementation study of facilitated planning recommended; farmer agreement is the open gate.
